subject: Dedicated GPU capacity recap & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@healthlink.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity recap & next steps

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap from our discovery call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag any inaccuracies.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes under concurrent inference during morning batch processing windows (95th pct spikes to ~1.2s with current setup).
- Risk profile: multi-tenant noisy neighbor concerns and requirement for tenant isolation for PHI-related workloads.
- Cost & predictability: need steady unit pricing for forecasting and committed capacity to avoid throttling during peak clinic hours.
- Compliance: SOC 2 and audit log retention for 12+ months, and customer-managed KMS for keys.

Goals we discussed:
- Dedicated, isolated GPU pool for core inference serving (reserved capacity).
- <100ms token latency SLO for single-request paths; 99.95% uptime target for the reserved pool.
- Autoscale/burst capacity for scheduled spikes (up to +50% for short windows).
- Proof-of-concept for isolation (network + tenant separation) before committing.

Redwood preliminary proposal (high level):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (we can map to H100 if you prefer HW parity).
- Private VPC endpoint + customer-managed KMS integration; audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
- Autoscale rule: warm baseline (4 nodes) with burst policy to 6 nodes for <30 min windows; soft fallbacks to a smaller model family if capacity constrained.
- SLA target on the pool: 99.95% availability, token latency guidance tied to request size and batch rules.

Attachments: MAP_HealthLink_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan draft) — contains milestones, owners, and tentative pricing bands.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Tech deep-dive: Marcus to run a throughput/latency estimate (I suggested Thu 04/15 10:00 AM PT).
2) Security checklist: we'll share an updated SOC 2 evidence pack + SAML/KMS integration notes.
3) POC scope: isolation validation + two-week load window for baseline metrics.
4) Commercial: ballpark pricing & SOW to be shared within 3 business days after TD.

Can you confirm 1) the priorities above (latency, isolation, predictability) and 2) availability for a technical deep-dive on Thu 04/15 10:00 AM PT?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive 
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

On Tue, Apr 12, 2026 at 2:05 PM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ethan —
> 
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap from our discovery call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag any inaccuracies.
> 
> [summary snipped]

Thanks for the clear recap, Soojin — adding some technical context so HealthLink has an engineering view ahead of the TD: 

Throughput/latency estimates (ballpark):
- Baseline model: LLM-2-8b (quant-friendly) — expect ~600-900 qps per A100-80GB equiv for short sequences (<=128 tokens) with continuous batching tuned to 40-60ms latency contribution from batch windowing.
- If you need <100ms end-to-end single-request latency, we recommend smaller single-request-optimized model variants or pre-warmed isolated nodes with minimal batching.

HW mapping and recommendation:
- Option A (cost balance): 4x A100-80GB equiv (reserved) + 2x burst nodes (same family).
- Option B (performance-heavy): 2x H100-PCIe + 2x A100 for mixed workloads (lower latency on critical routes).

Operational controls we recommend including in the MAP/SOW:
- Per-route routing: critical endpoints hit the reserved pool; background batch jobs hit a shared pool.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (can reduce token compute by 20–35% depending on hit rate).
- Canary rollout gating with traffic mirroring for model swaps.

Acceptance tests for the POC:
- Isolation smoke: concurrent tenant saturation test with telemetry proving no cross-tenant degradation.
- Latency window test: 95/99 latency profiles under 80% baseline and 120% burst.
- Audit/export: 12-month log retention proof and export to your SIEM.

Attachments: infra_sketch.png (rough layout of private VPC + peering + audit flow). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-HealthLink/infra-diagrams

I can pull together a concrete runbook and capacity-sizing doc before Thu if you want — happy to map test scenarios to HealthLink's morning batch profile.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@healthlink.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU capacity recap & next steps

Appreciate the fast follow-up and the level of detail — this matches what we discussed. A few quick confirmations/questions from my side: 

1) Priorities: confirmed — isolation and predictable performance come first, latency goal secondary (we can tune model variants once isolation is validated).
2) POC: we want an isolation POC that can run against a scrubbed subset of PHI (we'll coordinate with legal for data handling). Two-week window sounds right.
3) Security: please send the SOC 2 evidence pack and the SAML/KMS integration notes. We'll also need the standard vendor security questionnaire filled out (I'll attach ours in a follow-up).
4) Commercials: please send a preliminary SOW + ballpark quote. If we can see a committed baseline and a clear burst policy, procurement is likely to move quickly.

Availability: Thu 04/15 10:00 AM PT works for the TD. Let's lock it.

I'll loop in our procurement lead (cc'ing ops@healthlink.io) once we have the SOW draft.

Thanks — looking forward.

Ethan Shaw
Head of AI Ops
HealthLink
ethan.shaw@healthlink.io | +1 (617) 555-0228

Attachments: will follow with vendor questionnaire
